title: A Microfluidic Flow Chamber Model for Platelet Transfusion and Hemostasis Measures Platelet Deposition and Fibrin Formation in Real-time
protocol: Prepare the microfluidic flow chamber channels, tubing, and connecting pins.
Resuspend the collagen stock vial by vortex mixing.
Dilute resuspended collagen in isotonic glucose solution to a final concentration of 50 µg/mL.
Take a new, disposable microfluidic biochip with eight straight, parallel channels.
Label one end of the channel(s) as the outlet.
Pipette 0.8 µL of collagen into the outlet of the channel(s).
Fill 5/6 of the channel length with collagen.
Incubate the biochip at 4 °C for at least 4 h in a humidified and sealed container.
Dilute rhTF in 10 mM HEPES-buffered saline (HBS) to a final concentration of 9 pM.
Remove the collagen-coating solution via the outlet.
Pipette 0.8 µL of rhTF in HBS into the outlet of the channel, filling 5/6 of the channel length.
Incubate the biochip for an additional 30 min in a humidified and sealed container.
Fill the coated channels with blocking buffer starting from the inlet.
Fill an equal number of Y-shaped channels with the same blocking buffer in a mixing biochip.
Make sure all channels and channel arms are completely filled with blocking buffer.
Incubate both biochips for at least 1 h in a humidified and sealed container.
Prepare two tubing of 8 cm long, one 2 cm long, and one 46 cm long for each channel in use.
Place a pin in one end of the three smaller tubing and in both ends of the longest tubing.
Rinse all pump fluidics and the connected tubing with distilled water.
Degrease the biochip's casting with a precision dust-free wipe and denatured alcohol to remove prints and dust.
Fill all tubing with blocking buffer before connecting them to the biochips.
Fix the coated biochip on the automated microscope stage.
Fix the mixing biochip at the same height as the microscope stage using a laboratory scissor jack.
Connect the coated biochip with the mixing biochip using the longest tubing, 46 cm long.
Make sure both biochips are at a distance so that the tubing forms a flexible but straight line.
Attach a syringe connector pin into the Luer-compatible tubing of the rinsing pump.
Connect it to the free end of the 2-cm tubing and fix the other end to the outlet of the coated biochip.
Fix the two 8-cm tubing to the mixing biochip inlet using its pins.
Put the free end of each tubing in a vial of HBS.
Rinse all tubing and all channels with 1 mL HBS.
Open the driver software of the perfusion pumps.
Initialize the pumps by double-clicking on the syringes icon in the software.
Select the type of syringe that will be used: 1 mL syringes for the coagulation buffer and 2 mL syringes for the reconstituted blood.
Connect the syringes to the biochip construction.
Disconnect the rinsing pump and all tubing, except for the one connecting the two biochips.
Connect the 2-cm tubing with its syringe connector pin to the Luer lock of a thick-walled waste tubing.
Fill the thick-walled tubing with standard pepsin solution using a syringe.
Secure the open end of the thick-walled tubing with a Kocher clamp.
Place a suitable waste container with bleach underneath to collect the flow-through.
Fix the tubing with its pin to the outlet of the coated biochip.
Collect blood in an evacuated ethylenediamine-tetraacetic acid (EDTA) container.
Use the EDTA blood sample only for performing a complete blood count (CBC) using an automated hematology analyzer.
Collect 5 mL of blood in evacuated sodium citrate containers.
Place the collected samples on a horizontal rotator pending blood reconstitution.
Centrifuge the collected blood at 250 x g for 13 min to prepare platelet-rich plasma (PRP).
Transfer the PRP to a fresh conical centrifugation tube without using the brake to prevent pellet disturbance.
Centrifuge the PRP at 4,500 x g with brake for 10 min to pellet the platelets and prepare platelet-poor plasma (PPP).
Discard the platelet pellet after centrifugation.
Incubate the PPP in a water bath at 37 °C.
Transfer packed red blood cells to a fresh conical tube by perforating the bottom of the original one with a 21 G needle.
Determine the hematocrit of the packed red blood cells using an automated hematology analyzer.
Determine the platelet concentration of the platelet concentrate for analysis using an automated hematology analyzer.
Calculate the volume of packed red blood cells, platelet concentrate, and PPP to achieve a 40% hematocrit and 250 x 10^3 platelets/µL in a 2.5 mL final volume.
Mix these components to prepare reconstituted blood.
Perform a CBC on the prepared reconstituted blood.
Prepare a "blank" control sample by replacing the volume of platelet concentrate with an equal volume of saline.
Label the reconstituted blood for platelets and fibrinogen.
Pipette 13 µL of a 10.7 mg/mL solution of Alexa Fluor 405-labeled fibrinogen into a test tube (final concentration: 70 µg/mL).
Add 1 mL of reconstituted blood to the test tube containing labeled fibrinogen.
Mix another 1 mL of reconstituted blood with 2 µL of 1 mM DiOC6 (final concentration: 1 µM) or 2 µL of 5 mM Calcein AM (final concentration: 5 µM).
Add this mixture to the tube containing the blood and fibrinogen, resulting in a final volume of 2 mL.
Gently mix by inverting the tubes.
Incubate the sample for 10 min at 37 °C.
Prepare coagulation buffer containing 10 mM CaCl2 and 3.75 mM MgCl2 in HBS.
Filter-sterilize the coagulation buffer through a 0.2 µm filter.
Pre-warm the coagulation buffer to 37 °C.
Focus the microscope optics to the collagen fibers adhered to the bottom of the channel.
Select "Set current Z for selected tile regions" in the experiment software.
Define a region of interest (ROI) using the acquisition software of the microscope.
Mount a 1 mL syringe containing 1 mL of pre-warmed coagulation buffer in the perfusion pump.
Mix the pre-warmed reconstituted blood by gently inverting and load 2 mL into a 2 mL syringe.
Remove all air from both syringes.
Connect each syringe to an 8-cm tubing using a syringe connector pin.
Prime the connectors and tubing of both syringes at high speed (400 µL/min) until filled with coagulation buffer or blood.
Fix the other end of both tubing to the split legs of the Y-shaped channel in the mixing biochip, using pins.
Use the bottom leg for perfusing coagulation buffer and the upper leg for reconstituted blood.
Initiate perfusion at 4.4 µL/min for coagulation buffer and 44 µL/min for reconstituted blood.
Remove the Kocher clamp at the outlet of the waste tubing to permit perfusion.
Start a stopwatch to determine the time between the initiation of the experiment and the start of real-time image acquisition.
Record images every 10 seconds for 30 minutes in real time using the microscope's acquisition software.
Start recording when the mix of reconstituted blood and coagulation buffer enters the coated biochip mounted on the microscope stage.
Use a 100X magnification (10X objective and 10X lenses).
Terminate the pumps and image acquisition after 30 min or earlier if the signal is saturated.
Detach all tubing and syringes.
Discard tubing and syringes as biohazardous waste.
Determine thrombus growth kinetics using image analysis software.
Determine fibrin formation kinetics using image analysis software.
Open the plugin Processing: stitching to stitch side-by-side images per time point.
Open the Image Analysis plugin to determine surface coverage of platelets.
Define the region of interest by drawing a rectangle measuring 637 mm².
Select the tab All Views to include all recorded time points.
Use Create Tables to generate a spreadsheet with mean fluorescence intensity values for each time point.
Save the spreadsheets in xml format.
Open a spreadsheet in a spreadsheet program for further calculations.
Subtract the initial (background) value from all data.
Plot the fluorescent signal as a function of perfusion time for the green dye (platelets).
Plot the fluorescent signal as a function of perfusion time for the violet dye (fibrin).
Calculate the slope of platelet adhesion and accumulation by linear regression.
Determine the moment of onset for fibrin coagulation by extrapolating its slope to intercept the X-axis.
